title: Randomized cohort + shadow canary playbook for pinned model variants
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Problem: When customers pin a model revision, we need a safe, measurable way to introduce new versions behind that pin without breaking SLAs or degrading quality. Current pin workflows lack a standardized randomized cohort + shadow canary option that both validates correctness against control traffic and exercises production load patterns for latency/cost profiling. Goals: (1) Define a playbook and UI affordances for running randomized holdout cohorts with optional shadowing of requests to candidate model variants; (2) Publish required performance profiles and telemetry schemas so model onboarding teams can certify variants prior to promotion; (3) Provide automated gates (latency, error, quality drift, cost delta, safety heuristics) and an operator rollback/mitigation playbook; (4) Integrate with Console dashboards and rollout APIs so PMs/SEs can launch experiments without engineering changes.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with step-by-step runbook for randomized cohort + shadow canary flows
Console UI/CLI supports creating a pinned rollout that includes: percentage holdout cohorts, shadow-mode option, randomized assignment seed, and synthetic prompt injection for validation
Telemetry contract published: latency_p50/p95, token_cost_per_request, quality_delta_embedding_sim, safety_flag_rate, request_entropy metric; dashboards and alerts wired in runtime-1.22 release
Automated gate logic prototype implemented in staging that can auto-fail/rollback when thresholds exceeded; integration test demonstrating rollback on simulated regression
Two internal onboarding sessions run with Applied ML and Solutions Engineering to validate playbook and instrumentation
steps: Draft playbook with risk categories and rollback triggers
Define telemetry schema and sample queries for Console dashboards
Work with Applied ML to compile a canonical synthetic prompt set for canary validation
Implement randomized cohort assignment and shadowing controls in rollout API (ENG dependency)
Wire alerts and dashboard panels; create template for per-rollout observability
Run two shadow+holdout pilots with low-traffic customer accounts and capture metrics and learnings
risks: Randomized cohorts could introduce customer-facing variance if cohort assignment leaks across sessions
Shadowing increases token costs and KV cache usage—needs cost guardrails
Quality metrics for open-ended generation are noisy; embedding-based drift needs calibration and false-positive handling
Regulatory customers may require explicit consent/visibility for shadowing or synthetic prompt tests
mitigations: Use deterministic hashing by customer_id + seed to avoid cross-session churn and make cohorts sticky
Limit shadow traffic via budgeted envelope and autoscaling safety caps; require approval for >5% shadow rate
Build baseline calibration jobs to map embedding-drift to human-assessed quality delta before enabling auto-rollback
Expose consent flag and audit log entries for privacy-regulated workspaces; add opt-out in private deployments
decisions: Favor randomized cohort + shadow hybrid over pure canary for first phase to balance correctness and load profiling
Initial default gate thresholds: latency_p95 <= control_p95 + 30ms, error_rate delta < 0.1%, embedding_similarity_mean >= 0.92 relative to control
Shadow traffic will be sampled server-side and charged to an internal experiments budget until adoption
